claim: UHRF1 is a histone- and DNA-binding RING E3 ubiquitin ligase that recruits DNMT1 to sites of newly replicated DNA through ubiquitylation of histone H3.
source: The epigenetic inheritance of DNA methylation requires UHRF1, a histone- and DNA-binding RING E3 ubiquitin ligase that recruits DNMT1 to sites of newly replicated DNA through ubiquitylation of histone H3.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing UHRF1's role in DNA methylation inheritance.

claim: UHRF1 binds DNA with selectivity towards hemi-methylated CpGs (HeDNA).
source: UHRF1 binds DNA with selectivity towards hemi-methylated CpGs (HeDNA); however, the contribution of HeDNA sensing to UHRF1 function remains elusive.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing preferential binding to HeDNA and by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation.
source: Here, we reveal that the interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation but is dispensable for chromatin interaction, which is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation experiments showing that HeDNA-binding mutants cannot rescue DNA methylation loss.

claim: The interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is dispensable for chromatin interaction.
source: Here, we reveal that the interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation but is dispensable for chromatin interaction, which is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin fractionation experiments showing that HeDNA mutants retain chromatin binding.

claim: Chromatin interaction of UHRF1 is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains.
source: Here, we reveal that the interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation but is dispensable for chromatin interaction, which is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays showing mutual enhancement of histone and DNA binding.

claim: HeDNA recognition activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation towards multiple lysines on the H3 tail adjacent to the UHRF1 histone-binding site.
source: HeDNA recognition activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation towards multiple lysines on the H3 tail adjacent to the UHRF1 histone-binding site.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays and mass spectrometry data identifying multiple H3 lysine ubiquitylation sites.

claim: This study provides the first demonstration of a DNA-protein interaction directly regulating E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
source: Collectively, our studies are the first demonstrations of a DNA-protein interaction and an epigenetic modification directly regulating E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel finding that HeDNA binding stimulates UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.

claim: This study provides the first demonstration of an epigenetic modification directly regulating E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
source: Collectively, our studies are the first demonstrations of a DNA-protein interaction and an epigenetic modification directly regulating E3 ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel finding that DNA methylation status (HeDNA) regulates UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.

claim: UHRF1 plays a central role in DNMT1-directed DNA methylation maintenance during DNA replication.
source: The E3 ubiquitin ligase UHRF1 (ubiquitin-like, containing PHD and RING finger domains 1) is one such multi-domain epigenetic regulator (Figure 1A) that plays a central role in DNMT1-directed DNA methylation maintenance during DNA replication (Bostick et al., 2007; Sharif et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies establishing UHRF1's role in DNA methylation maintenance.

claim: UHRF1 functions through the reader activity of its linked TTD-PHD towards the N-terminus of histone H3 when it is di- and tri-methylated at lysine 9 (H3K9me2/me3).
source: It does so in part through the reader activity of its linked TTD-PHD (tandem Tudor and plant homeodomain) towards the N-terminus of histone H3 when it is di- and tri-methylated at lysine 9 (H3K9me2/me3) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), and through RING (really interesting new gene) domain-mediated catalysis of H3K18 and H3K23 ubiquitylation that promotes DNMT1 association with H3 (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: UHRF1 RING domain mediates catalysis of H3K18 and H3K23 ubiquitylation that promotes DNMT1 association with H3.
source: It does so in part through the reader activity of its linked TTD-PHD (tandem Tudor and plant homeodomain) towards the N-terminus of histone H3 when it is di- and tri-methylated at lysine 9 (H3K9me2/me3) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), and through RING (really interesting new gene) domain-mediated catalysis of H3K18 and H3K23 ubiquitylation that promotes DNMT1 association with H3 (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies on UHRF1 ubiquitylation activity.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a 10- to 20-fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA.
source: UHRF1 displayed a 10- to 20-fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA, and a 5- to 10-fold preference for HeDNA over SyDNA (Figure 1B; left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a 5- to 10-fold preference for HeDNA over SyDNA.
source: UHRF1 displayed a 10- to 20-fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA, and a 5- to 10-fold preference for HeDNA over SyDNA (Figure 1B; left panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The G448D mutation (DNAmut) disrupts all DNA-binding by UHRF1.
source: G448D (DNAmut) disrupts all DNA-binding (Figure 1B; middle panel) by installing a negatively charged residue at a position that contacts the DNA backbone (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and N489A (HeDNAmut), harbored within the NKR finger that contacts the unmethylated cytosine opposite the methylated base (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), disrupts only HeDNA-sensing (Figure 1B; right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays and structural analysis.

claim: The N489A mutation (HeDNAmut) disrupts only HeDNA-sensing by UHRF1.
source: G448D (DNAmut) disrupts all DNA-binding (Figure 1B; middle panel) by installing a negatively charged residue at a position that contacts the DNA backbone (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and N489A (HeDNAmut), harbored within the NKR finger that contacts the unmethylated cytosine opposite the methylated base (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), disrupts only HeDNA-sensing (Figure 1B; right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays and structural analysis.

claim: The DNA binding affinity of UHRF1 was exquisitely sensitive to small perturbations in salt concentration, with a nearly 500-fold affinity difference for HeDNA between 50 mM and 150 mM NaCl.
source: We also observed that the DNA binding affinity of UHRF1 was exquisitely sensitive to small perturbations in salt concentration; we measured a nearly 500-fold affinity difference for HeDNA between 50 mM and 150 mM NaCl (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays at different salt concentrations.

claim: Global DNA methylation levels were significantly reduced following stable knockdown of endogenous UHRF1 by shRNA.
source: Consistent with our previous observations (Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), global DNA methylation levels were significantly reduced following stable knockdown of endogenous UHRF1 by shRNA (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis of 5mC content in UHRF1 knockdown cells.

claim: DNA methylation was restored by reintroduction of a wild-type UHRF1 transgene.
source: DNA methylation was restored by reintroduction of a wild-type UHRF1 transgene, but like mutations that disrupt histone interaction through the PHD finger (H3mut; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (RINGmut) and DNA binding (DNAmut), HeDNAmut could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells despite retaining its ability to bind DNA (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HeDNAmut could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells despite retaining its ability to bind DNA.
source: DNA methylation was restored by reintroduction of a wild-type UHRF1 transgene, but like mutations that disrupt histone interaction through the PHD finger (H3mut; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (RINGmut) and DNA binding (DNAmut), HeDNAmut could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells despite retaining its ability to bind DNA (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation experiments and DNA binding assays.

claim: Hemi-methylated DNA sensing is critical for DNA methylation maintenance.
source: These results demonstrate that in addition to the well-appreciated roles of histone-binding and ubiquitin ligase activity to the DNA methylation regulatory function of UHRF1 (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), hemi-methylated DNA sensing is critical for DNA methylation maintenance.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation experiments showing HeDNAmut cannot rescue DNA methylation.

claim: Wild-type and HeDNAmut UHRF1 bound to bulk chromatin biochemically fractionated from HeLa cells.
source: Notably, unlike H3mut and DNAmut, wild-type and HeDNAmut bound to bulk chromatin biochemically fractionated from HeLa cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin association assays shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 perform complementary functions to target UHRF1 to chromatin.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 are performing complementary functions to target UHRF1 to chromatin, and that HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer in the DNA methylation program.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding but cannot rescue DNA methylation.

claim: HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer in the DNA methylation program.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 are performing complementary functions to target UHRF1 to chromatin, and that HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer in the DNA methylation program.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential requirements for chromatin binding versus DNA methylation function.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a preference for H3K9me3 peptides over unmodified H3 peptides.
source: In agreement with previous analyses of the isolated TTD-PHD (Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), full-length UHRF1 displayed a preference for H3K9me3 peptides over unmodified H3 peptides (H3K9un) (Figure 2A; top panel, see also Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays and citations to prior work.

claim: DNA binding enhances the interaction of UHRF1 with H3K9me3 and H3K9un peptides.
source: Histone binding measurements in the presence of 10 μM unlabeled HeDNA, SyDNA, or UnDNA enhanced the interaction with C-terminal FAM-labeled H3K9me3 and H3K9un peptides (Figure 2A; top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with DNA present.

claim: H3K9me3 peptide enhanced DNA binding affinity 5–10 fold irrespective of the methylation status on DNA.
source: Reciprocally, DNA-binding measurements in the presence of 10 μM unlabeled H3K9me3 peptide enhanced DNA binding affinity 5–10 fold irrespective of the methylation status on DNA (Figure 2B–C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with H3 peptide present.

claim: The histone- and DNA-binding modules of UHRF1 are regulated by reciprocal positive allostery.
source: Collectively, these experiments demonstrate that the histone- and DNA-binding modules of UHRF1 are regulated by reciprocal positive allostery.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays showing mutual enhancement of binding.

claim: The extent to which H3 peptides augmented the interaction of UHRF1 with DNA was dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3.
source: In agreement with the multivalent histone engagement model of the UHRF1 TTD-PHD, the extent to which H3 peptides augmented the interaction of UHRF1 with DNA was dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with different H3 peptide modifications.

claim: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of DNA binding over H3K9un.
source: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of DNA binding over H3K9un, and asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a), which blocks the UHRF1 PHD interaction with H3 (Rajakumara et al., 2011), did not enhance DNA binding (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays comparing different H3 peptides.

claim: Asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a) blocks the UHRF1 PHD interaction with H3.
source: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of DNA binding over H3K9un, and asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a), which blocks the UHRF1 PHD interaction with H3 (Rajakumara et al., 2011), did not enhance DNA binding (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and binding assays.

claim: H3R2me2a did not enhance DNA binding by UHRF1.
source: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of DNA binding over H3K9un, and asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a), which blocks the UHRF1 PHD interaction with H3 (Rajakumara et al., 2011), did not enhance DNA binding (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays.

claim: H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate DNA binding.
source: Consistently, H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate DNA binding, a previously characterized double mutation to the linker connecting the TTD-PHD that uncouples multivalent engagement to H3 (Linkermut) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013) exhibited a weaker enhancement of DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type, and DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with mutant proteins.

claim: Linkermut exhibited a weaker enhancement of DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type.
source: Consistently, H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate DNA binding, a previously characterized double mutation to the linker connecting the TTD-PHD that uncouples multivalent engagement to H3 (Linkermut) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013) exhibited a weaker enhancement of DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type, and DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with mutant proteins.

claim: DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3.
source: Consistently, H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate DNA binding, a previously characterized double mutation to the linker connecting the TTD-PHD that uncouples multivalent engagement to H3 (Linkermut) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013) exhibited a weaker enhancement of DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type, and DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with mutant proteins.

claim: The DNA binding affinity of HeDNAmut was enhanced by H3K9me3, although HeDNAmut could not discriminate between UnDNA and HeDNA.
source: Conversely, the DNA binding affinity of HeDNAmut was still enhanced by H3K9me3, although HeDNAmut could not discriminate between UnDNA and HeDNA (Figure 2C), providing a biochemical basis for HeDNAmut retention on chromatin (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays with HeDNAmut.

claim: The UHRF1 TTD-PHD associated with the SRA and SRA-RING in pull-down experiments.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, the UHRF1 TTD-PHD associated with the SRA and SRA-RING in pull-down experiments (Figure 3A), and this association was perturbed in the presence of DNA, irrespective of methylation status (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro pull-down assays shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The association between UHRF1 TTD-PHD and SRA-RING was perturbed in the presence of DNA, irrespective of methylation status.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, the UHRF1 TTD-PHD associated with the SRA and SRA-RING in pull-down experiments (Figure 3A), and this association was perturbed in the presence of DNA, irrespective of methylation status (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assays with DNA present.

claim: SRA-RING DNAmut maintained interaction with the TTD-PHD in the presence of DNA.
source: SRA-RING DNAmut maintained interaction with the TTD-PHD in the presence of DNA (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assays with the DNAmut protein.

claim: An H3K9me2 peptide did not inhibit the interaction between the SRA and the TTD-PHD.
source: However, an H3K9me2 peptide did not inhibit the interaction between the SRA and the TTD-PHD (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assays with H3 peptide present.

claim: The DNA-binding surface of the SRA contributes to an intramolecular interaction in a manner non-competitive with histone binding.
source: These results suggest that the DNA-binding surface of the SRA contributes to an intramolecular interaction in a manner non-competitive with histone binding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that DNA but not H3 peptide disrupts the TTD-PHD/SRA interaction.

claim: UHRF1 remained monomeric in the presence and absence of ligands as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography.
source: Indeed, UHRF1 remained monomeric and in good agreement with the expected molecular weight as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography, dynamic light scattering, and atomic force microscopy (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by analytical size exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: UHRF1 remained monomeric in the presence and absence of ligands as measured by dynamic light scattering.
source: Indeed, UHRF1 remained monomeric and in good agreement with the expected molecular weight as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography, dynamic light scattering, and atomic force microscopy (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by dynamic light scattering data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: UHRF1 remained monomeric in the presence and absence of ligands as measured by atomic force microscopy.
source: Indeed, UHRF1 remained monomeric and in good agreement with the expected molecular weight as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography, dynamic light scattering, and atomic force microscopy (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by atomic force microscopy data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide was observed in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Surprisingly, we observed robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) in a 20 min end-point assay in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate ubiquitylation activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values.
source: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate this activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values (Figure 4A), despite the ability of these DNAs to positively regulate histone binding (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Reduced ubiquitylation activity was observed as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM.
source: Consistent with our measured Kd for HeDNA (Figure 1B), we observed reduced ubiquitylation activity as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by HeDNA titration in ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: This is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction, and in particular an epigenetic modification, directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel finding that HeDNA binding stimulates UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.

claim: A 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was measured in the presence of HeDNA vs. UnDNA.
source: We measured a 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA vs. UnDNA, both in the presence or absence of H31-32K9me2 peptide (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurements shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA.
source: In sharp contrast, the rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurements shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
source: Comparing the rate of activity on UHRF1 substrates (peptide vs. self), the rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurements comparing auto-ubiquitylation and peptide ubiquitylation.

claim: The rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Conversely, the rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurements comparing auto-ubiquitylation and peptide ubiquitylation.

claim: HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
source: Based on these observations, we propose that HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential rates of auto-ubiquitylation versus peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA.

claim: UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA.
source: Similar to peptide substrates, UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), confirming that the enhanced ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 is relevant in the context of chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with mononucleosomes shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Excess H31-15K9me2 peptide effectively inhibited UHRF1 enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates.
source: In addition, when excess H31-15K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) (which harbors the TTD-PHD binding site but not the published ubiquitin target lysines) was added to UHRF1 mononucleosome ubiquitylation assays, H31-15K9me2 effectively inhibited enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with competing peptide shown in Figure 4C.

claim: HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation.
source: In contrast, HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation, consistent with its role as an activator of UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with excess HeDNA.

claim: The N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD.
source: These results suggest that the N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD and that DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that N-terminal H3 peptide inhibits nucleosome ubiquitylation.

claim: DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation.
source: These results suggest that the N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD and that DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that HeDNA does not block nucleosome ubiquitylation.

claim: HeDNA binding permitted robust formation of mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylated H3 peptides.
source: Reacting UHRF1 with peptide substrates, we observed low ubiquitin ligase activity in the absence of HeDNA, while HeDNA binding permitted robust formation of mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylated H3 peptides (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with mutant proteins shown in Figure 4D.

claim: DNA-, HeDNA-, and histone-binding loss-of-function UHRF1 mutants exhibited defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation, with the exception of D469G.
source: Characterizing DNA-, HeDNA-, and histone-binding loss-of-function UHRF1 mutants in ubiquitylation assays revealed defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation, with the exception of the previously reported SRA loss-of-function mutant (D469G) (Avvakumov et al., 2008), that exhibited wild-type binding to HeDNA in our assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with mutant proteins.

claim: The TTD-PHD is the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
source: Ubiquitylation defects observed for H3mut and Linkermut confirmed a critical role for the TTD-PHD as the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation and demonstrated that multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with H3mut and Linkermut.

claim: Multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation.
source: Ubiquitylation defects observed for H3mut and Linkermut confirmed a critical role for the TTD-PHD as the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation and demonstrated that multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with Linkermut.

claim: DNAmut UHRF1 showed complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation.
source: In addition, complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation for DNAmut UHRF1 and the absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3 for HeDNAmut UHRF1 further support the role of DNA binding and HeDNA recognition to fully activate UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with DNAmut.

claim: HeDNAmut UHRF1 showed absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3.
source: In addition, complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation for DNAmut UHRF1 and the absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3 for HeDNAmut UHRF1 further support the role of DNA binding and HeDNA recognition to fully activate UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays with HeDNAmut.

claim: Neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in affinity for E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA.
source: Surprisingly, neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in affinity for the E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC and NMR experiments shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was readily observed in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA.
source: In addition, we readily observed UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating the RING domain of UHRF1 could productively interact with E2-ub regardless of the methylation status of the bound DNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Ubiquitin retained its dynamics when bound to UHRF1.
source: Notably, upon E3 binding to the conjugated E2, NMR resonances belonging to the conjugated ubiquitin did not suffer as great a loss in intensity (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C), indicating that ubiquitin retained its dynamics when bound to the E3.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's.
source: This observation suggests that UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's (Christensen et al., 2007; Pruneda et al., 2011a, 2012).
evidence: This claim is inferred from NMR data and compared to prior studies on other E3 ligases.

claim: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA.
source: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 in these assays (monitored by the loss of the E2-ub and the appearance of free E2) showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: When an H31-20 peptide was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 was observed.
source: Remarkably, when an H31-20 peptide (Supplementary file 1) was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, we observed rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays with H3 peptide shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 was observed in ubiquitin discharge reactions.
source: Additionally, we observed the appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was observed when peptide was present.
source: Notably, we also observed a decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation formed when peptide was present, presumably because more ubiquitin was being transferred to H3 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess.
source: Thus, even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess, ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays with excess lysine.

claim: Neither H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin.
source: Neither the H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays with acetylated peptides shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20.
source: Additionally, rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 (Figure 5D), indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Additionally, rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 (Figure 5D), indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that acetylated peptides do not enhance E2-ub depletion.

claim: Reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with acetylated H3 peptides.
source: Consistent with our previous single turnover results (Figure 5C), reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with the acetylated H3 peptides (Figure 5D), supporting a model where HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays shown in Figure 5D.

claim: HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation.
source: Consistent with our previous single turnover results (Figure 5C), reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with the acetylated H3 peptides (Figure 5D), supporting a model where HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential accumulation of ubiquitylated products.

claim: Virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
source: It is worth noting that in all single and multiple turnover assays performed, virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assays without HeDNA.

claim: HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism and suggest that HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective ubiquitylation and discharge assay data.

claim: HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism and suggest that HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective ubiquitylation and discharge assay data.

claim: The only histone peptides enriched greater than ten-fold in HeDNA samples relative to UnDNA samples were derived from H3.
source: We first identified peptides that were enriched in the HeDNA sample relative to the UnDNA sample, and the only histone peptides that were enriched greater than ten-fold were derived from H3 (Supplementary file 2) (see Materials and methods for information about normalization and quantification).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis of ubiquitylated mononucleosomes.

claim: Ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA.
source: Consistent with our findings that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity, ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In addition to H3K18 and H3K23, H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub were heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA.
source: In addition to the previously identified sites H3K18 and H3K23, we also found H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide were identified.
source: We further identified abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site).
source: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site), and H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry spectral count analysis.

claim: H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub.
source: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site), and H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1.
source: Collectively these results suggest that H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1, but that UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry data showing H3K18ub is most abundant.

claim: UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail.
source: Collectively these results suggest that H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1, but that UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry identification of multiple ubiquitylated lysines.

claim: Changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation were observed in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Consistent with our model of HeDNA altering UHRF1 substrate preferences, we also observed changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation.

claim: A nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub was identified in the presence of HeDNA.
source: In particular, we identified a nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub, a solvent exposed lysine in the PHD near the C-terminus of a bound H3 peptide (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: An additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band was observed in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA.
source: Accordingly, we observed an additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E), corroborating our mass spectrometry results.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Several histone PTMs co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation.
source: We also identified several histone PTMs that co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2.
source: Additionally, several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3.
source: We confirmed this epigenetic link by immunoblotting HeLa mononucleosomes ubiquitylated by UHRF1. Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3, but not on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was not detected on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac.
source: We confirmed this epigenetic link by immunoblotting HeLa mononucleosomes ubiquitylated by UHRF1. Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3, but not on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM.
source: In addition, titrating recombinant human histones H3, H2A, and H2B into ubiquitylation assays revealed that while UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM, H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations, and H3K9me2 protein (synthesized by native chemical ligation) could be modified at even lower concentrations (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by histone titration ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations.
source: In addition, titrating recombinant human histones H3, H2A, and H2B into ubiquitylation assays revealed that while UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM, H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations, and H3K9me2 protein (synthesized by native chemical ligation) could be modified at even lower concentrations (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by histone titration ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3K9me2 protein could be modified at even lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
source: In addition, titrating recombinant human histones H3, H2A, and H2B into ubiquitylation assays revealed that while UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM, H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations, and H3K9me2 protein (synthesized by native chemical ligation) could be modified at even lower concentrations (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by histone titration ubiquitylation assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Taken together, these findings strongly support the role of H3K9 methylation in directing UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry and immunoblot data showing H3K9me enhances ubiquitylation.

claim: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities.
source: Building on recent studies connecting H3 ubiquitylation to DNMT1 recruitment (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Qin et al., 2015), we propose a model where UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding and chromatin association data.

claim: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome.
source: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome to copy parental DNA methylation patterns (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the HeDNA-stimulated ubiquitylation data and prior studies on DNMT1 recruitment.

claim: Coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction of UHRF1.
source: Rather, coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding.

claim: The avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
source: We propose that the avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding affinity measurements and allostery data.

claim: Small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD dramatically affect chromatin targeting of UHRF1.
source: This may also explain why small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD (e.g., Linkermut and TTD aromatic cage mutation [Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012]) so dramatically affect chromatin targeting of this protein.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the chromatin association data with mutants and cited prior work.

claim: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail.
source: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail (Figure 6B): this ability may be related to the complexities of PTM patterning found on this region of the H3 tail (Young et al., 2009) and the necessity to promote efficient recruitment of DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data showing multiple ubiquitylation sites.

claim: UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair).
source: In addition, UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair) (Liang et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citations to prior work on UHRF1 in DNA repair.

claim: DNMT1 has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates.
source: Important to note are studies on the enzymology of DNMT1 activity that show the enzyme has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates (Goyal et al., 2006) and methylates in a processive manner (Bestor and Ingram, 1983; Hermann et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior enzymology studies on DNMT1.

claim: DNMT1 methylates in a processive manner.
source: Important to note are studies on the enzymology of DNMT1 activity that show the enzyme has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates (Goyal et al., 2006) and methylates in a processive manner (Bestor and Ingram, 1983; Hermann et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior enzymology studies on DNMT1.

claim: UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
source: Considering DNMT1 behavior on oligonucleotide substrates, it is intriguing to speculate that UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
evidence: This claim is speculative and inferred from DNMT1 processivity and UHRF1 ubiquitylation data.

claim: HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
source: We speculate that HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on the observed HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation.

claim: RING activity towards H3 may be conformationally restricted when UHRF1 binds SyDNA or UnDNA.
source: RING activity towards H3 may be conformationally restricted when UHRF1 binds SyDNA or UnDNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on the differential ubiquitylation activity with different DNA substrates.

claim: Structures of the SRA domain from mouse UHRF1 (Np95) show this domain can adopt different conformations bound to UnDNA and HeDNA.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, structures of the SRA domain from mouse UHRF1 (Np95) show this domain can adopt different conformations bound to UnDNA and HeDNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) (Hashimoto et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior structural studies.

claim: The NKR finger of the UHRF1 SRA adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding.
source: Also the NKR finger of the UHRF1 SRA, which harbors the HeDNAmut, adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding (Avvakumov et al., 2008; Hashimoto et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The stable NKR finger conformation is critical for HeDNA-stimulated H3 ubiquitylation.
source: This allows for pseudo-base pairing to the exposed guanosine nucleotide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and we hypothesize this stable finger conformation is critical for HeDNA-stimulated H3 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on structural information and ubiquitylation data.

claim: The half-life of H2BK123ub in budding yeast is approximately one minute.
source: In fact, recent analysis of ubiquitin turnover kinetics showed that the half-life of H2BK123ub in budding yeast is approximately one minute (Yumerefendi et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on ubiquitin turnover.

claim: USP7 may be responsible for removing H3 ubiquitylation through interaction with DNMT1.
source: The initial study implicating H3 ubiquitylation in the inheritance of DNA methylation indirectly suggested that USP7 may be responsible for this function through interaction with DNMT1 (Nishiyama et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is speculative and based on citation to a prior study.

claim: USP7 has been shown to interact with UHRF1.
source: This is notable, as USP7 has also been shown to interact with UHRF1 (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Recent studies have tied USP7 to DNA replication.
source: Additionally, recent studies have tied USP7 to DNA replication (Lecona et al., 2016) and the maintenance of heterochromatin (Mungamuri et al., 2016), providing a biological link to replication-coupled inheritance of DNA methylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Recent studies have tied USP7 to the maintenance of heterochromatin.
source: Additionally, recent studies have tied USP7 to DNA replication (Lecona et al., 2016) and the maintenance of heterochromatin (Mungamuri et al., 2016), providing a biological link to replication-coupled inheritance of DNA methylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Direct evidence of USP7 catalyzed deubiquitylation of H3 is lacking.
source: However direct evidence of USP7 catalyzed deubiquitylation of H3 is lacking.
evidence: This claim is based on the absence of direct experimental evidence in the literature.
